caption: The drawing depicts a decorative doorway set in a stone wall. The doorway features a wooden door with a slightly arched top, vertical plank construction, and visible hardware such as metal studs and a door handle. The door is textured with wood grain details and shows a damaged or cut-out lower section on the left side. Surrounding the door, there are two prominent columns, one on each side, colored in earthy orange and brown tones, with base and capital details. Atop these columns are finials. Above the doorway, a decorative arch structure connects the columns, comprised of angular and curved elements with three ornamental finials, one at the center and one above each column, linked by curving string-like adornments. The wall behind these elements is rendered in muted, pale blue-green stone, textured with irregular lines suggesting aged stonework. The area below the doorway is a tiled or stone floor in similar earthy shades to the columns. The drawing has minimal background elements, focusing on the doorway and its architectural features. The lower right corner of the drawing contains the signature "HARRY H. MADBELL."
title: Mission Church Doorway
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
